brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 7.4% profit vs typical 5.0%, and we have four proven rigid-packaging alternates ready to qualify

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Bring the price down toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc for items like caps (market fair-price band shows headroom at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 7.4% of every rupee they sell vs 5.0% at similar firms — that extra 2.4 points of profit sits in the price. The open-market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec — so there's room to move down

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days earlier (15 days after receipt instead of current 30) in exchange for a 3.5% price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier ties up an extra ₹1.64 L of our cash; they borrow money at about 7.02%, so 15 days early is worth roughly 3.5% annualised to them — trade that for a matching price cut

brief.financialLeverage: PGP Glass is healthy and liquid: CARE A+ / Stable rating, ₹3373.51 Cr revenue, keeps 7.4% profit, and sits in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.45) but generates strong free cash flow of ₹2899.48 Cr. Their cash is stuck for 78 days vs 71 at similar firms, and they pay suppliers in 29 days vs peer 42 — so cash is slightly tighter than peers, but not distressed. We're tiny to them — ₹39.99 L is 0.01% of their sales — so on our own we have little pull. The play is to bundle this negotiation with qualifying one of the four strong alternates (Manjushree, Mold-Tek, Hitech, Pearl) so they know a second source is live, then push on price using their fat margin and on payment terms using their borrowing cost.

evidence.point: They keep 7.4% profit vs 5.0% at similar firms — 2.4 points more sits in the price
Strong credit rating means little risk they'll stumble — we can push harder
They borrow at about 7.02%, so paying 15 days early is worth roughly 3.5% annualised to them
We're a tiny customer — ₹39.99 L is 0.01% of their ₹3373.51 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck for 78 days vs 71 at similar firms — slightly tighter than peers

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100) — top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable — a robust alternate for bottles/closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded & blow-moulded packaging; broad capability across bottles/caps

risks: We're 0.01% of their revenue — on our own we have no leverage; bundle volume or commit multi-year to get their attention, and make sure one of the alternates is qualified and priced before this meeting
Two red flags on file: EPF payment delays and pending legal case(s) — ask them to explain and confirm no supply disruption

Altman Z score 1.45 puts them in the grey zone (not distress, but watch) — don't squeeze so hard that you tip a wobbly supplier; keep the tone on partnership and qualifying a second source for our own security
The market-ask verdict says 'MARKET-FAIR' with only modest headroom — so a 10–15% cut is ambitious; be ready to settle at 7–10% if they push back hard and show their own material costs
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a long-term partnership on rigid packaging, but we need your price to come down 10–15% to match the profit you're making above the market — and we're qualifying Manjushree and Mold-Tek as second sources to de-risk our supply.
